text: Let a be a positive real number such that $\int\limits _{0}^{a}e^{x-[x]}dx=10e-9$ where [ x ] is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Then a is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
a > 0

Let $n\leq a<n+1,n\in W$

 $a=\begin{array}{lll} [a] & + & \{a\} \\ ⇓ &  & ⇓ \\ G.I.F. &  & Fractionalpart \end{array}$

Here [ a ] = n

Now, $\int\limits _{0}^{a}e^{x-[x]}dx=10e-9$

$\Rightarrow \int\limits _{0}^{n}e^{\{x\}}dx+\int\limits _{n}^{a}e^{x-[x]}dx=10e-9$

$\therefore$ $n\int\limits _{0}^{1}e^{x}dx+\int\limits _{n}^{a}e^{x-n}dx=10e-9$

$\Rightarrow n(e-1)+(e^{a-n}-1)=10e-9$

$\therefore$ n = 0 and ${a} = \log _{e} 2$

So, $a=[a]+\{a\}=(10+\log _{e}2)$

$\Rightarrow$ Option (2) is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: The mean of 6 distinct observations is 6.5 and their variance is 10.25. If 4 out of 6 observations are 2, 4, 5 and 7, then the remaining two observations are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let other two numbers be a, (21 $-$ a)

Now,

$10.25=\frac{(4+16+25+49+a^{2}+(21-a)^{2}}{6}-(6.5)^{2}$

(Using formula for variance)

$\Rightarrow 6(10.25)+6(6.5)^{2}=94+a^{2}+(21-a)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow a^{2}+(21-a)^{2}=221$

$\therefore$ a = 10 and (21 $-$ a) = 21 $-$ 10 = 11

So, remaining two observations are 10, 11.

$\Rightarrow$ Option (1) is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: The value of the integral $\int\limits _{-1}^{1}\log _{e}(\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x})dx$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{-1}^{1}\log _{e}(\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x})dx$

We know, $\int\limits _{-a}^{a}f(x)dx=2\int\limits _{0}^{a}f(x)dx$

So, $2\int\limits _{0}^{1}\log _{e}(\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x})dx$

$l=2\int\limits _{0}^{1}\log _{e}(\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x}).1dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{2}=\log _{e}(\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x}).x]_{0}^{1}-\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1+x}}-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-x}}}{\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x}}.xdx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{2}=\log _{e}\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{1-x}-\sqrt{1+x}}{\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x}}\right )\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{2}=\log _{e}\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (\frac{(1-x)+(1+x)-2\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{(1-x)-(1+x)}\right )\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{2}=\log _{e}\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{2(1-\sqrt{1-x^{2}})}{-2x}.\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{2}=\log _{e}\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}-1\right )dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{2}=\log _{e}\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{2}[\sin ^{-1}x-x]_{0}^{1}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{2}=\log _{e}\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{π}{2}-1\right )$

$\therefore$ $l=\log _{e}2+\frac{π}{2}-1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 3 \\ a & 0 \end{array}\right ]$, a$\in$R be written as P + Q where P is a symmetric matrix and Q is skew symmetric matrix. If det(Q) = 9, then the modulus of the sum of all possible values of determinant of P is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 3 \\ a & 0 \end{array}\right ]$, $A^{T}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & a \\ 3 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$A=\frac{A+A^{T}}{2}+\frac{A-A^{T}}{2}$

Let $P=\frac{A+A^{T}}{2}$ and $Q=\frac{A-A^{T}}{2}$

$Q=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 0 & \frac{3-a}{2} \\ \frac{a-3}{2} & 0 \end{array}\right )$

Det (Q) = 9

$0-\left (\frac{3-a}{2}\right )\left (\frac{a-3}{2}\right )=9$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{a-3}{2}\right )^{2}=9\Rightarrow (a-3)^{2}=36$

$a-3=\pm 6\Rightarrow a=9,-3$

$P=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & \frac{a+3}{2} \\ \frac{a+3}{2} & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$P=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 6 \\ 6 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$ or $\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

 | P | = - 36 or 0

$\therefore$ | $-$36 + 0 | = 36
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text:
If z and $ω$ are two complex numbers such that $|zω|=1$ and $\arg (z)-\arg (ω)=\frac{3π}{2}$, then $\arg \left (\frac{1-2z–ω}{1+3z–ω}\right )$ is :

(Here arg(z) denotes the principal argument of complex number z)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As $|zω|=1$

$\Rightarrow$ If $|z|=r$, then $|ω|=\frac{1}{r}$

Let $\arg (z)=θ$

$\therefore$ $\arg (ω)=\left (θ-\frac{3π}{2}\right )$

So, $z=re^{iθ}$

$\Rightarrow z–=re^{iθ}$

$ω=\frac{1}{r}e^{i\left (θ-\frac{3π}{2}\right )}$

Now, consider

$\frac{1-2z–ω}{1+3z–ω}=\frac{1-2e^{i\left (-\dfrac{3π}{2}\right )}}{1+3e^{i\left (-\dfrac{3π}{2}\right )}}=\left (\frac{1-2i}{1+3i}\right )$

$=\frac{(1-2i)(1-3i)}{(1+3i)(1-3i)}=-\frac{1}{2}(1+i)$

$\therefore$ $prin\arg \left (\frac{1-2z–ω}{1+3z–ω}\right )$

$=prin\arg \left (\frac{1-2z–ω}{1+3z–ω}\right )$

$=\left (-\frac{1}{2}(1+i)\right )$

$=-\left (π-\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{-3π}{4}$

So, option (2) is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: Let [ x ] denote the greatest integer $\leq$ x, where x $\in$ R. If the domain of the real valued function $f(x)=\sqrt{\frac{|[x]|-2}{|[x]|-3}}$ is ($-$ $\infty$, a) $\cup$ [b, c) $\cup$ [4, $\infty$), a < b < c, then the value of a + b + c is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For domain,

$\frac{|[x]|-2}{|[x]|-3}$ $\geq$ 0

Case I :

When $|[x]|-2$ $\geq$ 0

and $|[x]|-3$ > 0

$\therefore$ x $\in$ ($-$ $\infty$, $-$3) $\cup$ [4, $\infty$) ...... (1)

Case II :

When $|[x]|-2$ $\leq$ 0

and $|[x]|-3$ < 0

$\therefore$ x $\in$ [$-$2, 3) ..... (2)

So, from (1) and (2) we get

Domain of function

= ($-$ $\infty$, $-$3) $\cup$ [$-$2, 3) $\cup$ [4, $\infty$)

$\therefore$ (a + b + c) = $-$3 + ($-$2) + 3 = $-$2 (a < b < c)

$\Rightarrow$ Option (3) is correct.

text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation $x\tan \left (\frac{y}{x}\right )dy=\left (y\tan \left (\frac{y}{x}\right )-x\right )dx$, $-1\leq x\leq 1$, $y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{π}{6}$. Then the area of the region bounded by the curves x = 0, $x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and y = y(x) in the upper half plane is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The equation gives

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y\tan (y/x)-x}{x\tan (y/x)}=\dfrac{y}{x}-\cot \left (\dfrac{y}{x}\right )$

With $y=vx$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$, so $x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=-\cot v$, that is $\tan v\qquad dv=-\dfrac{dx}{x}$.

Integrating, $\ln |\sec v|=-\ln |x|+c$. At $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$, $v=\dfrac{π/6}{1/2}=\dfrac{π}{3}$ and $\sec v=2$, so $\ln 2=\ln 2+c$ and $c=0$.

Hence $\cos \left (\dfrac{y}{x}\right )=|x|$, and on $0<x\leq \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ the solution through $\left (\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{π}{6}\right )$ is $y=x\cos ^{-1}x\geq 0$, which lies in the upper half plane.

$\text{Area}=\int\limits _{0}^{1/\sqrt{2}}x\cos ^{-1}xdx=\left [\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\cos ^{-1}x\right ]_{0}^{1/\sqrt{2}}+\dfrac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1/\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx$

The first term is $\dfrac{1}{4}\times \dfrac{π}{4}=\dfrac{π}{16}$. With $x=\sin θ$, $\int\limits _{0}^{1/\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx=\int\limits _{0}^{π/4}\sin ^{2}θdθ=\left [\dfrac{θ}{2}-\dfrac{\sin 2θ}{4}\right ]_{0}^{π/4}=\dfrac{π}{8}-\dfrac{1}{4}$.

$\text{Area}=\dfrac{π}{16}+\dfrac{π}{16}-\dfrac{1}{8}=\dfrac{π-1}{8}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ be three mutually perpendicular vectors of the same magnitude and equally inclined at an angle $θ$, with the vector $\vec{a}$ + $\vec{b}$ + $\vec{c}$. Then $36\cos ^{2}2θ$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}\right |^{2}=\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}+\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}+\left |\vec{c}\right |^{2}+2(\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{a}.\vec{c}+\vec{b}.\vec{c})=3$

$\Rightarrow \left |\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}\right |=\sqrt{3},\vec{a}.(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})=\left |\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}\right |\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow 1=\sqrt{3}\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow \cos 2θ=-\frac{1}{3}$

$\Rightarrow 36\cos ^{2}2θ=4$

text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r_{1}}=α\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}+λ(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\widehat{k})$, $λ$ $\in$ R, $α$ > 0 and $\vec{r_{2}}=-4\hat{i}-\widehat{k}+μ(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\widehat{k})$, $μ$ $\in$ R is 9, then $α$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If $\vec{r}=\vec{a}+λ\vec{b}$ and $\vec{r}=\vec{c}+λ\vec{d}$ then shortest distance between two lines is 

$L=\frac{(\vec{a}-\vec{c}).(\vec{b}\times \vec{d})}{|b\times d|}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}-\vec{c}=((α+4)\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\widehat{k})$

$\therefore$ $((α+4)\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}).\frac{(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\widehat{k})}{3}=9$

or $α$ = 6

$C_{2}\to C_{2}-C_{3}$

text: If the value of $\lim _{x\to 0}(2-\cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x})^{\left (\frac{x+2}{x2}\right )}$ is equal to $e^{a}$, then a is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}(2-\cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x})^{\frac{x+2}{x2}}$

form : $1^{$\infty} $=e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{1-\cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}{x2}\right )\times (x+2)}$

Now, $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{1-\cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}{x^{2}}=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x\sqrt{\cos 2x}-\cos x\times \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\cos 2x}}\times (-2\sin 2x)}{2x}$ (by L' Hospital Rule)

$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x\cos 2x+\sin 2x.\cos x}{2x}=\frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{3}{2}$

So, $e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{1-\cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}{x2}\right )(x+2)}$

$=e^{\frac{3}{2}\times 2}=e^{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ a = 3
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift
